Division 07 Roofing Subcontractor for Lancaster County General Contractors

General contractors bidding work across Lancaster County's mix of manufacturing, healthcare, education, and municipal projects need a roofing sub who can turn a bid package around on schedule and hold to it once the job starts. Commercial Roofing Contractors of Lancaster prices, submits, and executes Division 07 scope on new construction, renovation, and tear-off and replacement projects, from single-building bids to phased multi-building contracts.

Bid Packages, Submittals, and Division 07 Scope

We price off the drawings and specifications as issued, flag ambiguities through RFIs before bid day rather than after award, and return submittals with cut sheets, shop drawings where applicable, and manufacturer data matched to the spec section as written. On prevailing wage projects, we carry the certified payroll and wage documentation required without it becoming a separate coordination burden for your office.

Where a specified system has a long lead time or a limited installer network in this market, we flag it during the bid phase and propose an approved-equal substitution request early enough for your team to review it before it affects the schedule.

For larger institutional bid packages, hospital additions, school renovations, or multi-building government contracts, we'll walk the site with your estimating team before bid day when access allows, since roof condition assessment done in person catches deck and drainage issues that don't always show up on existing drawings.

New Construction Roofing vs. Renovation and Tear-Off Scope

New construction roof scope is straightforward in one sense: no existing conditions to work around, but coordination with structural steel, mechanical rooftop unit placement, and other trades setting curbs and penetrations on your schedule, not ours. We track those interfaces closely so roof dry-in doesn't get held up waiting on a curb from another trade, and so we're not the reason a building can't be enclosed on schedule.

Renovation and tear-off projects carry the opposite risk profile: existing deck conditions, legacy penetrations, and asbestos-containing roofing materials on older Lancaster County building stock that weren't always fully documented in pre-bid site information. We do a pre-construction roof walk on renovation work whenever access allows, so unknown conditions surface before mobilization instead of as a field change order in week two.

On projects where a building needs to stay partially operational during renovation, whether that's a working manufacturing bay or an occupied wing of a larger campus, we build phasing into our proposal from the start rather than treating occupied-building coordination as a condition discovered once mobilized.

Schedule Coordination on Multi-Trade Job Sites

Roofing sits on the critical path on most projects: nothing interior can proceed reliably until the building is watertight. We staff crews to hold committed dry-in dates, communicate weather-driven schedule risk early rather than the day it becomes a problem, and coordinate crane and material hoist windows with other trades working the same site logistics plan.

  • Ground-up new construction Division 07 scope
  • Renovation and phased reroofing on occupied or partially occupied buildings
  • Tear-off and full replacement on existing structures
  • Roof recover and overlay scope where specified
  • Metal panel and standing seam installation on new steel buildings
  • Rooftop equipment curb and penetration coordination with mechanical trades

On projects with a compressed schedule, we'll propose sequencing options at the bid stage rather than waiting until the project is underway to raise a schedule concern.

Manufacturer Warranty and Closeout Documentation

Closeout packages on commercial roofing include manufacturer warranty registration, as-built documentation, O&M manuals, and any inspection or certification paperwork required by the specified system. We assemble that package to match your closeout schedule rather than treating it as a loose end after substantial completion, since a delayed warranty registration is one of the more common items that holds up final payment on a roofing line item.

Where a project requires a manufacturer-inspected installation for an extended warranty term, we schedule that inspection during the work, not after, so any correction needed doesn't become a punch list item discovered weeks later.

Change Orders and Field Condition Reporting

When we find a deck condition, deteriorated substrate, or existing system that doesn't match bid documents, we document it with photos and a written scope description before pricing a change, and we get that in front of your project manager as soon as it's found rather than batching field issues for later. That keeps your owner conversations grounded in specific documented conditions instead of general allowances.

During construction, RFIs on roof-related details, parapet height changes, equipment curb relocations, drainage modifications requested by other trades, get a same-week response from us whenever possible, since a stalled roof RFI can hold up dry-in for the whole building enclosure.

Common Questions from GCs Bidding Division 07 Scope

Do you carry certified payroll for prevailing wage projects?

Yes. We maintain the wage and certified payroll documentation required on Pennsylvania Prevailing Wage Act and Davis-Bacon projects and submit it on your required schedule.

How quickly can you turn around a bid on a Division 07 package?

Turnaround depends on scope and drawing completeness, but we prioritize bid deadlines on projects where we're a serious contender and will tell you upfront if a deadline isn't realistic given the information provided.

What happens if you find asbestos-containing material during tear-off on a renovation project?

We stop work in the affected area, document the condition, and notify your project manager immediately so it can be handled through the proper abatement process before roofing work resumes there.

Can you hold a committed dry-in date on a tight schedule?

We staff to the committed date at bid and flag weather or supply risk to that date as early as possible, rather than waiting until the date is missed to raise it.

Do you provide as-built roof documentation for the closeout package?

Yes, including manufacturer warranty registration, O&M documentation, and as-built roof plans matched to your project's closeout requirements.
